Present a scene to a room#

Walk clients through a flat, a showroom or a product together: everyone opens the same room link, you take the floor, their cameras follow yours, your voice reaches them from where your avatar stands, and every tour step, hotspot, material variant, light change and section cut you make appears on their screens as you make it.

You need: a scene link (any share link works, public or private) and a room name. No account; the room name is the only secret, so pick one nobody will guess (showflat-42-tue-3pm, not demo).

1. Open the room#

Add ?room=<name> to the scene link and send it round. Each viewer can add &as=<their name>; otherwise they appear as "guest". The **viewers panel** (bottom right) lists everyone in the room with a coloured dot — the same colour as their in-world avatar.

Up to 32 viewers share a room. Everyone sees everyone's avatar move live.

2. Talk#

Click Join voice. The browser asks for the microphone once. From then on:

  • Mute / Unmute your own microphone.
  • Open mic ↔ Push-to-talk: with push-to-talk, hold T (or the Hold to talk button) while you speak.
  • Spatial ↔ Stereo: by default each voice comes from where that person's avatar stands and fades with distance (useful in a large flat); Stereo plays everyone flat and at full level.
  • Mute next to a name silences that one person for you only.

The dot next to a name pulses while they speak, and their avatar brightens in the scene. "muted" next to a name means they muted themselves.

Voice is peer-to-peer between the browsers: nothing is recorded and no audio passes through the Verse server (only the connection handshake does). Two limits follow from that:

  • Six talkers per room. A seventh person who joins voice sees "Voice is limited to 6 talkers" and hears nothing; viewers who do not join voice are not counted. For larger audiences, present with voice among the six and let the rest watch.
  • Direct connections first, a relay when the server has one. Most home and office networks connect directly. Phones on mobile data (carrier NAT) and strict corporate firewalls often cannot; voice then goes through a TURN relay if the server has one configured (see Tour together § Voice). Without a relay, a pair that cannot connect sees "No audio with <name> — the network blocks a direct connection"; a phone hotspot or a different network on one side fixes it. Everything else in the room keeps working.

Add &voice=1 (open mic) or &voice=ptt to the link to join voice as the page opens.

3. Present#

Click Present in the viewers panel (or open the link with &present=1). For everyone else:

  • their camera glides to yours and stays with it — you walk, they walk;
  • a veil over their viewport says Following <you> with two buttons: Take control (their own camera again; a Rejoin the presenter chip brings them back) and Raise hand;
  • your Play tour, hotspot jumps, Variant, Lights and Section changes happen on their screens too;
  • the point under your pointer is drawn for them as a red laser dot.

A raised hand pulses that person's row in your panel for a few seconds. Hand over next to a name makes them the presenter (you start following them); Stop presenting gives everyone their camera back. If someone else clicks Present while you are presenting, they take over — the panel tells you.

4. In an embed#

The same room works inside your own page through the embed SDK:

Code
const viewer = Verse.embed(el, { model: "ingest/<id>.vpk" });
viewer.joinRoom("showflat-42", { name: "Alex", voice: true });
viewer.present(true);                       // take the floor
viewer.on("speaking", (s) => roster.mark(s.id, s.speaking));
viewer.on("peer", (p) => p.state === "hand" && toast(`${p.name} raised a hand`));
viewer.on("room", (r) => r.state === "notice" && toast(r.message));

The follower veil, laser dot and the presenter's actions all render inside the frame; setVoice({ muted, pushToTalk, talking, spatial }) drives the voice knobs from your own controls. Reference: embed-sdk.md.

Good to know#

  • Rooms are memory-only on the server: a restart empties them and everyone's page reconnects by itself.
  • Voice needs HTTPS (or localhost) — browsers do not expose the microphone on plain HTTP.
  • Voice uses the WebRTC and Web Audio panner APIs every current browser ships; the automated gate exercises Chromium, so treat Safari and Firefox as "should work, not yet proven".
  • Headsets (WebXR) show the avatars and hear the voices; presenting from inside a headset is not offered.
